evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 84: L. Cassius identidem in causā quaerere solēbat, cui bonō fuisset (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “to whom for a good?”. The dative of purpose: alicui bonō esse, to be of benefit to someone.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
